memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: On the twelfth day Ahira son of Enan, the leader of the people of Naphtali, brought his offering. His offering was one silver plate and one silver sprinkling bowl, both filled with the finest flour mixed with olive oil as a grain offering; one gold dish filled with incense; one young bull, one ram and one male lamb for a burnt offering; one male goat for a sin offering; and two oxen, five rams, five male goats and five male lambs to be sacrificed as a fellowship offering. This was the offering of Ahira son of Enan. - Num 7:78-83 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
On the twelfth and final day, Ahira of Naphtali brought his offering. He came last of all the tribal leaders — but his gift was just as full, just as generous, and just as carefully recorded as the very first. Being last did not make him least.

There is real encouragement here for anyone who feels like they are always at the back of the line. Ahira waited eleven days while others went ahead of him. Yet when his turn finally came, God gave his offering the same full attention and honour as Nahshon's on day one. The last was not overlooked.

We often think being first is best, and being last is somehow lesser. But in God's eyes, the timing of our turn does not change the value of our devotion. Whether you serve early or late, whether you are noticed first or come quietly at the end, God receives your offering fully.

Jesus turned the world's ranking upside down when He said, "the last will be first, and the first will be last" (Matt 20:16). In God's kingdom, there is no scramble for position. The one who comes humbly last is honoured just as much as the one who leads.

If you feel you are always waiting your turn, always at the back, take heart. Your day will come, and when it does, God will receive your gift with full honour. Nothing offered to Him is ever second-rate in His sight.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Do you feel like you are always "last in line"?
- How does it comfort you that God honours the last as much as the first?
- Can you serve faithfully even while you wait your turn?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that being last does not make me least in Your eyes. Help me to serve faithfully whenever my turn comes, trusting You to receive my offering fully. Amen.
